# Results — Study 365 (Lottery / MAX effect): does the flashy tail underperform?

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw (2011)
**MAX** sort — rank the cross-section each month by each name's **highest single-day return
over the prior month**, form quintiles, and go **long the low-MAX (boring) names, short the
high-MAX (lottery) names** — tested on a **transparent large-cap proxy**. True MAX is a
CRSP-universe (thousands of names, small-caps included) object; yfinance gives only a
large-cap slice, so we run the sort on a fixed **S&P-100-style basket** and call it a proxy
throughout. Offline core + synthetic control are deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Lottery losers?" `BUSTED`

The lottery effect says investors over-pay for stocks with a big recent one-day pop, so the
flashy tail should **underperform**. On this large-cap survivor proxy it does the **opposite,
significantly**: the high-MAX quintile (Q5) returned **+29.8%/yr** vs the low-MAX quintile
(Q1)'s **+12.2%/yr**, so the textbook long-low / short-high book *loses* **−17.6%/yr** at HAC
**t = −3.44**. The sign holds across tertile/quintile/decile cuts and in both halves of the
sample. The published anomaly is real in CRSP small-caps; on liquid, surviving large-caps the
"lottery" sort just re-labels the decade's high-beta growth winners (the AAPL/NVDA/TSLA/AMD
tail), so it **inverts**. `NONE` on Signal (the claimed low-MAX edge is absent — what's
significant is the wrong sign, and it is **survivorship**), `MIRAGE` on Tradability (the only
significant spread is a negative beta/survivorship artefact, not a deployable lottery short),
and `BUSTED` on the folklore.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — a fixed **S&P-100-style 66-name large-cap basket** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**5,385** trading days; **21.4** years; partial 2026-06 bar dropped) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last complete month-end); inputs fingerprint `5c0c1743c8d7` |
| Signal | **MAX** = highest single daily return over the prior calendar month, per name, at month-end |
| Sort | rank cross-section by MAX → quintiles Q1 (low) … Q5 (high); equal-weight next-month return |
| Trade | long Q1 (low-MAX) / short Q5 (high-MAX), monthly; 1-month signal ⇒ full monthly turnover |
| Costs | 20 bps one-way per leg × turnover + 50 bps/yr short borrow on the high-MAX leg |

> **Proxy + survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A fixed ~66-name surviving
> large-cap basket is the *least* lottery-prone slice of the market — the opposite end from
> the small, illiquid names where Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw find the effect. On survivors, a high
> MAX last month flags the high-beta names that subsequently led the bull market, so the sort
> measures **momentum / beta of survivors**, not lottery-buying. The bias points *against* the
> anomaly here, and we say so: this tape can show the published effect **does not survive** the
> large-cap, survivor universe — it cannot certify the CRSP small-cap result either way.

## The cross-section — the flashy tail *won*, monotonically the wrong way

256 monthly cross-sections (2005-01 → 2026-04). Each quintile's next-month return,
equal-weighted, annualised:

| quintile | MAX rank | mean / yr | vol | Sharpe |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | **lowest** MAX (boring) | +12.2% | 12.6% | 0.97 |
| Q2 | | +11.7% | 14.4% | 0.81 |
| Q3 | | +14.9% | 16.8% | 0.89 |
| Q4 | | +13.3% | 20.1% | 0.66 |
| Q5 | **highest** MAX (lottery) | **+29.8%** | 26.3% | **1.13** |

The lottery story predicts Q1 ≫ Q5. Here Q5 nearly **triples** Q1's return and posts the
*highest* Sharpe — the high-MAX tail is the bull market's beta winner, not a value trap.

## The trade — long low-MAX / short high-MAX loses, significantly

| book | mean / yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | win-rate | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 − Q5 (long low-MAX, short high-MAX), **gross** | **−17.6%** | −0.78 | **−3.44** | 42% | 1.00 |
| Q1 − Q5, **net** (20 bps/leg + 50 bps/yr borrow) | −22.9% | −1.01 | **−4.48** | 39% | 1.00 |

The textbook lottery trade doesn't merely fail to pay — it is **significantly negative**
(HAC *t* = −3.44), with a sub-50% win-rate and a placebo *p* of ≈1.00 (a positive-mean draw is
essentially never beaten because the real mean is firmly negative). Costs and borrow make it
worse, but they are not the story: the **sign** is the story.

## Robustness — the inversion is not a quintile artefact

| cut | n | mean / yr (low − high) | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| tertiles (Q1 − Q3) | 256 | −10.8% | −2.69 | 41% |
| **quintiles (Q1 − Q5)** | 256 | **−17.6%** | **−3.44** | 42% |
| deciles (Q1 − Q10) | 256 | −27.2% | −4.10 | 39% |

The harder you cut into the tails, the **more negative** the low-minus-high spread — the
opposite of a vanishing edge. The high-MAX extreme is exactly where the survivor winners live.

| sub-period | n | mean / yr | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005–2015 | 132 | −12.6% | −1.61 |
| 2016–2026 | 124 | −22.9% | −3.58 |

Negative in **both** halves (stronger in the FANG-led second half) — not a single-regime fluke.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly panel with a **planted lottery penalty** (high-MAX names made to
underperform next month by ``edge`` × standardised MAX) confirms the sort + inference recover a
*real* low-minus-high edge when one is present, and find **nothing** when it is absent:

| planted edge | Q1 − Q5 mean / yr | HAC *t* | win-rate | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | −0.1% | −0.06 | 49% | 0.520 |
| **+0.002** (real lottery penalty) | +5.7% | **+3.98** | 59% | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the harness sits at *t* = −0.06 (no false positive); with a modest
planted penalty it turns the spread positive and clears *t* = 2. So the machinery is honest:
the **negative** *t* on the real tape is a genuine feature of the large-cap survivor
cross-section, not a coding artefact, and a *real* lottery effect would have shown up as a
clean **positive** spread had one existed here.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed low-MAX outperformance is **absent** on this tape; the
  significant spread runs the **wrong way** (Q1 − Q5 = −17.6%/yr, HAC *t* = −3.44), and that
  inversion is driven by **survivorship + large-cap beta** (high-MAX = the decade's growth
  winners), named on the Signal axis. The published CRSP small-cap anomaly is not reproduced
  — and cannot be certified — on a surviving large-cap universe.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The only statistically real spread here is a *losing* one; the
  textbook lottery short is negative gross and worse net of 20 bps/leg + 50 bps/yr borrow.
  There is no deployable low-minus-high MAX edge on these names.
- **"Lottery losers"? — BUSTED.** On liquid, surviving large-caps the flashy one-day-pop tail
  did **not** underperform — it posted the highest return *and* the highest Sharpe. The lottery
  morality tale is a small-cap / illiquid phenomenon that does not generalise to the names most
  retail investors actually hold.
